subject: SLA: Tiered remedy allocation and latency exception request
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@cloudforge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline & remedy allocation for pilot

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. CloudForge is keen to move to a 3-month pilot, but procurement flagged two items we need to reconcile before signing: uptime baseline and the monthly remedy calculation. A few specific asks: 

- Baseline uptime: we need a 99.95% commitment for the pilot (our app is customer-facing and we can't accept a 99.9% baseline).
- Monthly remedy: we prefer a tiered remedy pool (remedy dollars allocated per month with no single-event cap) rather than a pro-rated credit formula — helps our finance team with predictability.
- Latency SLO: p95 under 350ms for text generation (for the pilot scope).

I attached our internal SLA questions (CloudForge_SLA_Questions.pdf). Can Redwood offer an exception to standard template to accommodate these? If there are tradeoffs you need (commitment level, dedicated capacity, or higher monthly charge), let us know the options and numbers.

--
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Ops, CloudForge
maya@cloudforge.com
ops@cloudforge.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline & remedy allocation for pilot

Hi Maya —

Really appreciate the clear asks and the write-up. We can be flexible for pilots, but there are a few constraints we need to be explicit about so we don't over-index on tail risk across the fleet. Summary of Redwood's position and a pragmatic compromise we can take to legal/procurement today: 

1) Baseline uptime
- Redwood hosted standard: 99.9% monthly availability.
- Exception path: For a Dedicated or Reserved-pool pilot we can commit to 99.95% for a 3-month pilot if CloudForge agrees to: either (a) a 30% uplift on the monthly reserved fee for the pilot, or (b) a 6-month minimum commitment with standard monthly pricing. The uplift compensates for capacity/operational reserve.

2) Monthly remedy model
- Standard: pro-rated monthly service credits (credit = (1 - actual_uptime/guaranteed_uptime) * monthly_fee), capped at 100% of the monthly fee.
- Pilot concession (tiered remedy pool): we can implement a tiered ladder for the pilot only (3 months):
  * uptime >= 99.95% — no remedy
  * 99.5% <= uptime < 99.95% — remedy = 10% of monthly fee
  * 99.0% <= uptime < 99.5% — remedy = 25% of monthly fee
  * uptime < 99.0% — remedy = 50% of monthly fee (capped at 50% for pilot)
  This preserves predictability for CloudForge and limits single-event exposure for Redwood during a short pilot.

3) Latency SLOs
- We can commit to p50/p95 targets for the pilot region and workload shape you demonstrated, but they must be scoped to the agreed traffic profile (max sustained QPS) and include standard maintenance carveouts. For text gen: p95 <= 350ms is achievable on Dedicated pools for the pilot if you accept the uplift or 6-month commit above.

4) Maintenance & carveouts
- Scheduled maintenance windows (up to 4 hours/month per-region) will not count toward availability. We will include an explicit maintenance schedule in the amendment and provide 72-hour advance notice for non-emergency work.

5) Next steps & docs
- I've attached an initial amendment draft (RDW_SLA_Amendment_v1.docx) that captures the pilot ladder and the uplift option.
- If CloudForge prefers the remedy pool to be escrow-style (pre-funded pool) rather than crediting post-event, we can discuss mechanics with Finance.

I'll loop in Solutions (Marissa) and Sales Ops (Logan) on the numbers. Marissa — can you confirm the uplift % and an illustrative monthly fee so we can model the 30% number for CloudForge? Logan — please add any bill-of-materials comments (marketplace fees, reserved pool sizing).

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the amendment. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance after reviewing your ladder: 

- The uplift path is acceptable as long as the uplift is a fixed % for the pilot and presented as a single line-item; CloudForge prefers the uplift vs. a longer term minimum. Can you confirm the uplift is exactly 30% for the configured reserved pool in the attachment?
- Remedy pool: procurement prefers a pre-funded remedy pool for the pilot (escrow) rather than post-hoc credits — it helps with month-to-month cash flow and avoids accounting reversals. We propose funding a pool equal to 50% of one month’s reservation fee at start of pilot; any unused funds are returned or applied to the next month. Is that workable?
- Maintenance carveouts: please add language that clarifies emergency maintenance (security patches) will have a max of 2 unplanned windows/quarter that can be called without advanced notice, and these will be reported in the monthly availability report.

If you can confirm the uplift % in writing and update section 3 (remedy mechanics) to add the escrow option with the funding amount, we can get legal to run it. I also added a short comment in RDW_SLA_Amendment_v1.docx (see Drive link).

We'd like to finalize terms by Monday so we can start the pilot next week.

Regards,
Maya
